title: Convolutional Neural Networks
overview: Convolutional layers slide small shared filters over an image, exploiting locality and translation structure. They need far fewer parameters than fully connected layers on images.
objectives: Explain weight sharing, stride, padding and pooling

method.title: Convolution
method.body: Each filter computes a dot product over a local patch, producing a feature map.

method.title: Shape arithmetic
method.body: Output size = floor((n + 2p - k) / s) + 1 per spatial dimension.

method.title: Pooling
method.body: Max or average pooling downsamples feature maps and adds small translation tolerance.

method.title: Hierarchy
method.body: Early layers detect edges and textures; deeper layers combine them into parts and objects.

pseudocode:
for each output position (i, j):
    patch = x[i*s : i*s+k, j*s : j*s+k]
    out[i, j] = sum(patch * kernel) + bias
out_size = (n + 2*p - k) // s + 1

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
img = np.arange(36, dtype=float).reshape(6, 6)
kernel = np.array([[1, 0, -1], [1, 0, -1], [1, 0, -1]], dtype=float)  # vertical edge
k, s = 3, 1
n = (img.shape[0] - k) // s + 1
out = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        out[i, j] = (img[i*s:i*s+k, j*s:j*s+k] * kernel).sum()
print("output shape:", out.shape)
print(out)
